2_Introduction: The PSCs demonstrated improved PCE of 0.76% (with FF of 26.55%, VOC of 0.16 V, and JSC of 17.66 mA/cm²). A stable precursor mixture was achieved by taking a Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 solution (1.75 mol/L) as the base. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s, respectively. During the second spin coating step, 120 µL of CB was deposited onto the perovskite film 10 s before the program ended. The films were then annealed at 100 °C for 30 min. Spectral analysis indicates that, upon the onset of annealing, the film reaches the explosive nucleation point at 8.6 seconds, at which the photoluminescence (PL) intensity attains its maximum. Following this peak, the PL intensity decreases to 30% of its maximum value, with an average decay slope of 5.604583333.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite film's crystallization dynamics, governed by the triple-cation Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 composition and high precursor concentration, were precisely controlled through a two-step spin-coating process culminating in chlorobenzene antisolvent dripping, which triggered rapid supersaturation and directed nucleation during the final spin stage, followed by thermal annealing to promote grain growth and densification. The photoluminescence spectral analysis provides direct evidence of these crystallization kinetics, where the PL intensity maximum at 8.6 seconds after annealing onset marks the explosive nucleation point, after which the subsequent decay to 30% of the peak intensity with an average slope of 5.60 signifies the progression of crystal growth and the concomitant introduction of non-radiative recombination centers, likely stemming from point defects and grain boundary formation in the absence of targeted passivation. This uncorrected defect landscape, along with potentially suboptimal interfacial charge extraction, directly limited device performance, yielding a power conversion efficiency of 0.76% with an open-circuit voltage of 0.16 V, a short-circuit current density of 17.66 mA/cm², and a fill factor of 26.55%.
